title: kms-residency-reconciler-and-audit-anchoring-shim
author: Lena Fischer
release_notes: Add KMS residency reconciler middleware and audit anchoring shim to enforce per-tenant key-region constraints at runtime; no customer-visible API changes; rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see edge cases where a subset of operator requests (e.g. cross-zone operator automation and retry plumbing) can surface non-conforming KMS usage that bypasses residency enforcement and produces audit records with missing residency claims. This PR implements a runtime reconciler + audit anchoring shim that (1) intercepts KMS-bound operations, verifies effective region claims against tenant residency policy, and emits canonical anchored audit events, and (2) provides a lightweight reconciliation job for drifted operator credentials to detect and optionally quarantine KMS requests that violate configured residency constraints.

Summary of changes (single-string description):
- Add src/crypto/kms/residency_reconciler.go: middleware that checks KMS request context for tenant-region claim, consults residency cache, and rejects or routes to fallback KMS bindings.
- Add src/crypto/kms/anchored_audit_writer.go: produces compact, canonical audit envelopes with residency assertion, signer meta, and short-proof hash for downstream retention.
- Extend src/auth/rbacv2/policy_loader.go to expose policy TTL and region-assertion helpers; small API surface used by reconciler.
- Helm: deploy/helm/templates/kms-residency-configmap.yaml and values.swagger to enable feature-flagged rollout and tuning knobs (quarantine thresholds, reconciliation window).
- Docs: docs/security/kms-residency.md with operator-facing configuration and migration notes.
- Tests: tests/integration/test_kms_residency.sh and unit tests under internal/crypto/kms for edge-case coverage.

Design notes:
- Residency cache: a read-mostly in-memory cache refreshed via async subscriber to policy service; TTL made configurable to balance timeliness and performance.
- Decision semantics: if tenant policy marks region STRICT and request region mismatches, the reconciler will either reject the request (default) or, if in permissive rollout, tag the request as QUARANTINED and allow it through to a region-fallback KMS provider.
- Audit anchoring: every reconciler decision emits an anchored audit envelope containing request-id, tenant-id, decision, and a short-proof HMAC_SHA256 over the claim digest. Anchored envelopes intended for downstream compliance indexer to dedupe and reconstruct timeline even when upper layers drop tracing.
- Backwards compatibility: rollout behind feature flag kms_residency_reconciler=true. When disabled, code paths are no-op and audit writer emits legacy audit records.

Small illustrative snippet (residency_reconciler.go):
    // verifyRegion compares the request's claimed region to tenant policy
    if policy.Strict && reqRegion != policy.AllowedRegion {
        emitAnchoredAudit(ctx, req, "reject", "region_mismatch")
        return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "tenant residency violation: request region %s not allowed", reqRegion)
    }

Review conversation (selected threads):
- Marco Diaz (reviewer): "Can you clarify the performance budget here? the reconciler will be on the hot path for token issuance and small RPCs -- we should avoid extra network calls. Consider making policy cache default TTL 30s and prefer local evaluation."
  - Author (Lena Fischer): "Agreed. Default TTL set to 30s, reconciler uses in-process cache and async refresh. Fallback to the policy service only on cache-miss. Added benchmarking numbers in unit test comments."

- Priya Nair (reviewer): "Audit envelopes look good; need to make sure the proof HMAC key rotation is handled. How will old proofs be validated after rotation?"
  - Author: "Added signer_id into envelope and a signer-rotation table in deploy/helm/README; the compliance indexer will accept previous signer public keys for 7 days after rotation. Documented in docs/security/kms-residency.md (section 'Key rotation and proof validation')."

- Ethan Cole (reviewer): "Integration test intermittently fails on CI due to test container time drift. Suggest you make test resilient to up to +-120s offset and use monotonic clocks where possible."
  - Author: "Addressed; tests now normalize time windows and rely on monotonic timers for reconciliation window asserts. Re-ran CI locally and fixed flakiness."

- Security review (automated): "Static analysis flagged potential log injection in anchored audit writer when emitting free-form operator notes."
  - Author: "Sanitized operator notes via auditSanitize() and added a unit test for escaping. See commit 5e6f7g8."

CI summary: 
- build: pass
- unit: pass (all tests)
- integration: initial run failed (test_kms_residency.sh timing), rerun -> pass
- lint: pass with minor style adjustments applied

Rollback / migration plan (short):
- Start feature-flagged rollout in canary region (us-west-2) with permissive mode so that violating requests are quarantined but not rejected. Monitor anchored-audit indexer for QUARANTINED events and false positives.
- If spike in false positives: flip to off and collect samples; apply policy corrections; re-enable with longer TTL or widened quarantine window.
- Full rollout to main after 48hr canary with <0.1% false positive rate and no increase in 5xx for KMS proxy.

Operational notes:
- Adds a new metric: kms_residency.reconciler.decisions{decision=(accept|quarantine|reject)} and a histogram for decision latency.
- Anchored audit events are emitted to the same audit topic but include header X-Audit-Anchored: true; indexer config updated to pick up these events for compliance queries.

Merge outcome: Squash merged by Priya Nair on 2026-01-20. Changelog and release notes entry added under releases/notes/2026-01-20-kms-residency.md.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Performance regression on hot paths. Mitigation: in-process TTL-backed cache, synthetic perf tests included, and rollout behind feature flag.
- Risk: Incorrectly quarantining valid operator automation. Mitigation: permissive rollout and detailed anchored-audit payload for rapid triage.

Contact: For followups contact @lena-f or @security-team.
